rows.selection_reason: No experiments are completed yet, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple unimodal baseline has useful predictive signal and what performance level should be used as a reference. config_001 tests the simplest RNA-only, single-profile PCA pipeline, isolating basic RNA representation before adding image data, multiprofile aggregation, or fusion. It is the best first experiment because it is low-cost, establishes a baseline for RNA encoder and profile-setting comparisons, and avoids assuming that multimodal or multiprofile complexity will help.

The only completed experiment is an RNA-only, single-profile PCA baseline with validation accuracy 0.485 and F1 0.464, so there is currently no evidence about whether image features are informative. config_010 tests a simple image-only ResNet50 single-profile baseline, isolating the contribution of the image modality without introducing multiprofile aggregation or fusion complexity. This is the best next use of budget because it reduces uncertainty about whether multimodal modeling is likely to be worthwhile and establishes a reference point for later image-encoder and fusion comparisons.

RNA-only PCA singleprofile is currently the strongest result (0.485 accuracy, 0.464 F1), while image-only ResNet is much weaker (0.208 accuracy, 0.172 F1), suggesting RNA is the more promising direction. The key uncertainty is whether the PCA representation is already adequate or whether a learned RNA encoder can improve performance. config_004 tests this directly by changing only the RNA encoder from PCA to SCVI n200 while keeping singleprofile and avoiding image, fusion, or multiprofile complexity. This is a simple, high-information extension of the best baseline and is a better use of limited budget than jumping to more complex multimodal or multiprofile settings.

Existing evidence is sparse: RNA-only scvi_n200 singleprofile is the best result so far (0.520 accuracy, 0.498 F1), PCA RNA is weaker (0.485, 0.464), and image-only ResNet50 is weak (0.208, 0.172). The key uncertainty is whether another RNA representation, scgpt, can improve over the current best RNA encoder. config_007 tests scgpt under the same singleprofile RNA-only setting, isolating the representation choice without adding profile, aggregation, or fusion complexity. This is the best next use of budget because it directly reduces uncertainty about an important design decision and identifies the strongest RNA baseline before testing more complex multiprofile or multimodal configurations.

Existing single-profile RNA results show scvi_n200 is the strongest RNA encoder (0.520 accuracy, 0.498 F1), while PCA and scGPT are weaker and ResNet50 image-only is weak. The main uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation can improve the best RNA representation. config_005 extends config_004 by adding multiprofile with simple avgpool, isolating the profile/aggregation effect without adding fusion or a transformer. This is the best next experiment because it tests an important design choice on the strongest RNA encoder, may improve performance directly, and will clarify whether more complex aggregation or multimodal fusion is worth testing next.

The strongest completed result is config_005, RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool, reaching 0.650 accuracy and 0.628 F1, clearly above the single-profile scvi result and other RNA encoders. The main remaining uncertainty within this promising direction is whether transformer aggregation can improve on simple avgpool for the same multiprofile scvi representation. config_006 tests exactly that by changing only aggregation while keeping the best-known model, profile, and encoder fixed. This is an efficient next experiment because it exploits the current best evidence, likely has high expected performance, and isolates the effect of aggregation before investing in more complex multimodal configurations.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile scVI RNA is strong (~0.65 accuracy), while the only image-only test, ResNet50, is weak (~0.21). This leaves important uncertainty about whether the image modality can be useful at all or whether the weak result is due to a poor image encoder. config_013 tests a stronger pretrained image representation, ImageNet ViT-L, under the same simple image-only/single-profile setting, directly comparing to config_010. This is the best next experiment because it isolates image representation without changing profile setting, aggregation, or fusion, reducing uncertainty before spending budget on more complex multimodal fusion. If ViT-L improves image-only performance, it motivates multimodal ViT-L experiments; if not, it supports focusing on RNA-only multiprofile designs.

The strongest evidence is that RNA multiprofile with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation is much better than single-profile RNA models, especially compared with scvi_n200 single-profile and pca_n2000 single-profile. The key uncertainty is whether this gain comes from the multiprofile/transformer design generally or specifically from the scvi_n200 representation. config_003 keeps model setting, profile setting, and aggregation fixed while changing only the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to pca_n2000, directly isolating the representation effect. This is a high-value one-factor experiment before spending budget on more complex multimodal fusion choices.

The strongest evidence is that RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 models reach ~0.65 validation accuracy, with transformer aggregation slightly ahead of avgpool, while image-only single-profile models are weak and ViT is marginally better than ResNet. The key uncertainty is whether image features add complementary signal to the already strong RNA multiprofile representation. config_038 tests this by adding an ImageNet ViT image branch to the best RNA multiprofile transformer setup using simple concat fusion, giving a direct comparison to the RNA-only baseline config_006. This is the best next use of budget because it exploits the strongest known direction while testing the most important unresolved design question: whether multimodal fusion improves performance over the best RNA-only model.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile scvi RNA is strong (~0.65 accuracy), image-only models are weak, and the only multimodal test so far (config_038: scvi, ViT-L, transformer, concat) reaches 0.721 accuracy with supporting F1, suggesting that multimodal fusion is promising but only concat has been evaluated. This experiment tests whether weighted fusion improves over concat while keeping the RNA encoder, image encoder, profile setting, and aggregation fixed. It is the best next experiment because it directly extends the current best configuration, isolates the fusion design choice, and has high expected performance while reducing uncertainty about how to combine modalities under a limited budget.
